title: Graph construction of the global Frobenius operator
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
and the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and let $(K,\varphi)$ be a
strict Weil complex of
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex]. For $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ let
$\Phi^m$ be the $m$-fold iterate of the
scheme Frobenius of
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius] and
$u_m:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ the
scheme-Frobenius map of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map], and consider the
graph correspondence of [def-trf-graph-correspondence]
$c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$ with $u_m$. Then its
global operator $T_c(u_m)$ of
[def-trf-global-operator], identified as in
[prop-trf-graph-operator], equals the $m$-th iterate of the
global geometric Frobenius:

$$
T_c(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}:
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where $F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ is the endomorphism of the
global geometric Frobenius
operator of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] with its finite-coefficient compact-support transport
of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. The equality is natural in
$(K,\varphi)$ and compatible with the cocycle law in $m$.

Here the comparison $\kappa^{(m)}$ is the canonical one: using
$\Phi^m=g_\gamma^m\operatorname{Fr}_X^{(q^m)}$ from
[prop-trf-frobenius-factorization], it is the composite, with the canonical pullback-composition identification of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition],
$$
L\Phi^{m*}\simeq L(\operatorname{Fr}_X^{(q^m)})^*Lg_\gamma^{m*}
\xrightarrow{\ t_X^{(am)}\ }Lg_\gamma^{m*},
$$
where $t_X^{(am)}$ is the multiplicative absolute-Frobenius
trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. In particular it
uses the canonical constant-coefficient identifications, with no
scalar rescaling.

More generally, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry no Weil structure and
let $v:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\to K$ be an arbitrary morphism, not necessarily
invertible. Then the graph correspondence $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$
with $\kappa^{(m)}$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]
and coefficient map $v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ has

$$
T_c\bigl(v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K\bigr)
=R\Gamma_c(X,v)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}:
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^{m*}K)$
is the compact-support base-change isomorphism along $g_\gamma^m$; the
displayed identity $T_c(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ is the case $v=\varphi^{[m]}$.

proof.text:
Write $P_m=L\Phi^{m*}$, $G_m=Lg_\gamma^{m*}$ and $H=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$. The scheme map $\Phi$ is the scalar-extended $q$-power Frobenius constructed in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Its finiteness is the assertion of [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial], applied to the same finite-field datum and finite-type model $X_0$; this assertion requires neither reducedness nor separatedness of the model. Its iterates are proper without any new finiteness lemma: the identity is proper (its diagonal is an isomorphism, it is of finite type, and every base change is the identity). If $\Phi^r$ is proper, apply clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] to the finite map $f=\Phi$ and the proper map $h=\Phi^r$; the composite is $\Phi^{r+1}$. Induction gives properness for every $r\geq0$. For any $w:P_mK\to K$, [prop-trf-graph-operator] therefore gives
$$T_{(\mathrm{id},\Phi^m)}(w)=H(w)\circ e_{m,K},$$
where $e_{m,K}:H(K)\to H(P_mK)$ is the pullback/direct-image unit followed by proper coincidence and compact-support composition, exactly as specified by [def-trf-global-operator].

source.place: Opening paragraph: properness and expansion of the graph operator

proof.text: Choose a compactification $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow\bar X_0$ over $k_0$ by [prop-compactification-refinement] applied to $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Its base change is $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$: on underlying open subschemes it identifies $X$ with the inverse image of the open $X_0\subset\bar X_0$, since the fiber product of an open subscheme is exactly that inverse-image open. The base-changed compactification has proper structure map by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. A bounded constructible finite-coefficient complex has an etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] applies to $K$ and to its Galois pullbacks. Set $M=j_!K$ and write $C_K:H(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\bar X,M)$. By [lem-trf-compactification-graph-operator], for every $w:P_mK\to K$, the operator of Step 1 is conjugate under $C_K$ to the proper graph operator with coefficient map $\bar w=j_!w\circ b_{\Phi,m}$, where $b_{\Phi,m}:L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!\simeq j_!P_m$. The finite-Tor assertion $M\in D^b_{ctf}(\bar X,A)$ is supplied directly by [lem-trf-open-ctf].

source.place: Step 2: compute the specified compact-support maps in a compactification

proof.text:
On $\bar X$ put $\bar P_m=L\bar\Phi^{m*}$ and $\bar G_m=L\bar g^{m*}$. The comparison $\bar\kappa_m$ is the canonical factorization/trivialization comparison specified in the statement. Apply [lem-trf-graph-frobenius-unit-comparison] to $Y_0=\bar X_0$ and $M=j_!K$, which is bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude by Step 2. It identifies the actual ordinary cohomology maps, with the constant section $1$ preserved:
$$R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar\kappa_{m,M})\circ\rho_{\bar\Phi^m,M}=\rho_{\bar g^m,M}.$$
Here $\rho$ is the pullback/direct-image unit followed by the ordinary direct-image/global-sections identification. This equality is natural in $M$.

source.place: Step 1: identify the canonically normalized ordinary cohomology pullbacks

proof.text: Keep the semilinear base relation $\bar a\bar g^m=g_s^m\bar a$. Apply [lem-trf-graph-frobenius-point-exchange] to $\bar X_0$ and $M=j_!K$. It states exactly that ordinary exchange followed by the specified point transport is $\rho_{\bar g^m,M}$ in $D(A)$, including its normalization. The power square can equally be regarded as the one-step square for the degree-$m$ subfield of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]: base-changing $\bar X_0$ to that subfield leaves its geometric fiber unchanged and replaces $q$ by $q^m$ and $g$ by $g^m$. Thus the ordinary part of the compactification exchange in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] is this same map. No $k$-linearity of $\bar g^m$ is used.

source.place: Step 2: ordinary exchange and point transport on the same proper compactification

proof.text:
For the base-changed open $j$, [lem-trf-graph-frobenius-open-exchange] gives
$$b_{G,m}\circ\bar\kappa_{m,j_!K}=j_!\kappa^{(m)}_K\circ b_{\Phi,m}.$$
Item 2 of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] defines compact-support exchange as ordinary exchange on $j_!K$ followed by $R\bar a_*(b_{G,m})$. Substituting Step 4 into that definition and then the point-transport composite of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] gives
$$C_{G_mK}\circ\tau_{m,K}=R\Gamma(\bar X,b_{G,m,K})\circ\rho_{\bar g^m,j_!K}\circ C_K.$$
All maps use the compactification chosen in Step 2; the formula for a different representative is exactly the conjugation formula in the exchange definition. The map $\tau_{m,K}$ is invertible by [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso], applied to the datum $q^m$ as in Step 4.

source.place: Step 2: open comparison and the chosen-compactification formula

proof.text:
Let $v:G_mK\to K$ be arbitrary and put $w=v\kappa^{(m)}_K$. On the compactification, Step 2 gives $\bar w=j_!v\circ j_!\kappa^{(m)}_K\circ b_{\Phi,m}$. Substituting the open-comparison equation of Step 5 and the section-map equation of Step 3, the graph formula of [prop-trf-graph-operator] on the proper scheme $\bar X$ becomes
$$T_{\bar c}(\bar w)=R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!v)\circ R\Gamma(\bar X,b_{G,m})\circ\rho_G.$$
Here proper coincidence [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] identifies the compact-support graph formula with ordinary cohomology, using the identity compactification; no semilinear Galois map is treated as a $k$-endomorphism in that formula. Step 5 identifies the right side, after conjugation by $C_K$, with $H(v)\tau_{m,K}$. Naturality of $C$ from [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] and the graph intertwining of [lem-trf-compactification-graph-operator] therefore give
$$T_c(v\kappa^{(m)}_K)=H(v)\tau_{m,K}.$$
No Weil datum or inverse of $v$ has entered this argument, so this proves the full arbitrary-coefficient-map assertion.

source.place: Step 3: arbitrary coefficient maps, without invertibility

proof.text:
For a strict Weil complex take $v=\varphi^{[m]}$. The definition [def-trf-iterated-weil-map] gives $u_m=\varphi^{[m]}\kappa^{(m)}_K$. Step 6 and [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description] then give
$$T_c(u_m)=H(\varphi^{[m]})\tau_{m,K}=F_{c,K}^{\,m}.$$
For a morphism $a:(K,\varphi)\to(L,\psi)$ of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], the defining morphism condition is $a\varphi=\psi G_1(a)$, giving the case $m=1$. If $a\varphi_K^{[r]}=\psi_L^{[r]}G_r(a)$, the defining iterates give, under the canonical pullback-composition identifications,
$$a\varphi_K^{[r+1]}=a\varphi G_1(\varphi_K^{[r]})=\psi G_1(a\varphi_K^{[r]})=\psi G_1(\psi_L^{[r]})G_{r+1}(a)=\psi_L^{[r+1]}G_{r+1}(a).$$
Thus the intertwining identity holds for every $m\geq1$. Naturality of $\kappa^{(m)}$ and of $\tau_m$ gives $H(a)H(\varphi_K^{[m]})\tau_{m,K}=H(\psi_L^{[m]})\tau_{m,L}H(a)$, which is the asserted naturality.

source.place: Step 2: specialization to the strict Weil map and naturality

proof.text:
Use the same model compactification for every power. The successor formula of [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition] says
$$\tau_{r+1,K}=\tau_{1,G_rK}\tau_{r,K},\qquad\tau_{1,K}=\tau_{c,K},$$
with the canonical pullback-composition maps of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] understood. The base $r=1$ and this recursion identify $\tau_r$ with the $r$-fold one-step transport. They also imply
$$\tau_{m+n,K}=\tau_{m,G_nK}\tau_{n,K}\quad(m,n\geq1).$$
Indeed the case $m=1$ is the successor formula at $n$. If the identity holds at $m$, the successor formula at $m+n$ gives $\tau_{m+n+1,K}=\tau_{1,G_{m+n}K}\tau_{m,G_nK}\tau_{n,K}$; applying that same successor formula to $G_nK$ identifies its first two factors with $\tau_{m+1,G_nK}$. This proves the induction and identifies the direct degree-$r$ transport with the iterated transport of [def-trf-frobenius-operators].

Item statement: two recorded corrections, both confirmed. (1) The source's def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius reference takes E-coefficients, so it cannot act at finite A; it is replaced by the finite-A transport, and nothing is weakened. (2) The canonical comparison is the composite through the factorization and the absolute-Frobenius trivialization. I checked the factorization on rings: g∘Fr = Φ. Steps: Step 1 gets properness of every Frobenius iterate from finiteness and permanence (c) by induction. Step 2 gets the compactification, an étale-origin witness and j_!K in D^b_ctf, and graph intertwining holds for every coefficient map w. Steps 3–6 combine the three new comparisons on the proper compactification. I re-derived the chain T(\bar w) = RΓ(j_!v)RΓ(b_G)ρ_{\bar g}, which gives T_c(vκ) = H(v)τ_m without inverting v. Step 8 correctly extends the existing successor-only composition lemma to the two-index law. Steps 9–10 have the correct order and domains. proof_deps equals the union of step uses, every cited id exists and none is merged, and there is no cycle. New nodes: all three are statement-only, self-contained, searched with all three kinds of tool, and carry the correct blueprint.from. None restates a clause of the item. Unit comparison: true, and checked at Y=Spec k, M=A, m=1. Point exchange: true; on Y=s the exchange is the identity and ι(1)=1⊗1. Open exchange: true, because the source is an extension by zero, so equality is detected on X, where the exchanges are identities and κ restricts. An rg duplicate search over the DAG (pod proper-coincidence-frobenius, pur Frobenius-trivialization pullback, scheme-galois coefficient change, open-exchange section adjunct and others) found no duplicate. Edge cases: empty X, K=0, v=0, m=n=1, F_3 with ±κ, and dual numbers. No SGA source is used. I accepted the off-unit tool_uses listed in review.md.
